edges.mechanism: Quercetin (and rutin) activated P-gp and CYP3A4, cutting cyclosporine (Neoral) Cmax 67.8% and AUC 43.3%; authors advise transplant patients to avoid co-use (rejection risk).
edges.evidence: Rat PK study plus in vitro; 2026 SR notes P-gp interactions among the few clinically shown; low certainty

edges.mechanism: P-gp modulation: quercetin raised digoxin Cmax 413% and AUC 170% in pigs; 2 of 3 pigs at 50 mg/kg died. Human P-gp inhibition shown with fexofenadine.
edges.evidence: Animal PK study plus human probe study; no human digoxin data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Case report of enhanced anticoagulant effect; quercetin metabolites displace warfarin from albumin (weak CYP2C9 inhibition); additive antiplatelet activity.
edges.evidence: Case report (title only, no abstract) plus in vitro and human platelet data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Quercetin inhibits collagen-induced platelet aggregation in humans; isoquercetin inhibits PDI and lowers D-dimer and thrombin generation. No major bleeding in trials.
edges.evidence: Human pilot study and phase II/RCT biomarker data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Quercetin metabolites (isorhamnetin, tamarixetin) enhanced aspirin's antiplatelet effect more than additively, cutting aspirin IC50 about 10-fold.
edges.evidence: In vitro and whole-blood ex vivo assays; very low certainty for clinical bleeding

edges.mechanism: Inhibition of intestinal P-gp: 500 mg three times daily for 7 days raised fexofenadine AUC 55% and Cmax 68%.
edges.evidence: Human crossover PK study (n=12); moderate certainty for PK effect

edges.mechanism: Direction varies by substrate: P-gp inhibition (fexofenadine) vs lower talinolol exposure (induction or OATP uptake effects), more marked in ABCB1 3435 TT.
edges.evidence: Human PK studies (n=10-18); low certainty

edges.mechanism: OATP1B1 inhibition: 500 mg/d for 14 days raised pravastatin AUC 24% (CI 15-32%) and Cmax 31%; OATP1B1/1B3 Ki about 8-18 uM in vitro.
edges.evidence: Human PK study (n=16) plus in vitro; moderate certainty for PK effect

edges.mechanism: CYP2C9 inhibition: 500 mg twice daily for 10 days raised diclofenac Cmax/AUC beyond 0.80-1.25 limits and lowered 4-OH-diclofenac.
edges.evidence: Human open-label PK study (n=12); 2026 SR lists CYP2C9 among confirmed interactions; low-moderate certainty

edges.mechanism: Repeated quercetin induced CYP3A: lower oral midazolam AUC (500 mg/d x 13 d; 1500 mg/d x 7 d GMR 0.82), more in CYP3A5*1 carriers.
edges.evidence: Human PK studies (n=10-18); low certainty

edges.mechanism: Rapamycin is a CYP3A/P-gp substrate; quercetin induced CYP3A in humans and lowered exposure to the CYP3A/P-gp substrate cyclosporine in rats. Inferred; no sirolimus study.
edges.evidence: Mechanistic inference from human CYP3A probe and rat cyclosporine data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: CYP1A2 inhibition: 500 mg/d for 13 days lowered CYP1A2 activity 10.4% (CI 1.1-29.8%) and significantly slowed caffeine metabolism, regardless of CYP1A2*1C/*1F genotype.
edges.evidence: Two human probe studies (n=12 each); moderate certainty for PK effect, minor clinical impact

edges.mechanism: Quercetin inhibits COMT and MRP1, decreasing EGCG methylation and raising tissue EGCG 2-3x.
edges.evidence: Cell and mouse data only; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Quercetin binds DNA gyrase B (ATP site) but competes only weakly with quinolones; high-dose quercetin partly reduced ciprofloxacin activity against E. coli.
edges.evidence: In vitro only; clinical relevance unknown; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Quercetin chelates iron (3-OH/4-carbonyl) and lowers duodenal ferroportin, reducing basolateral iron export.
edges.evidence: Rat and Caco-2 data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Possible additive glucose/insulin lowering (insulin WMD -1.07; FPG lower only in >=500 mg/d, >=8 wk subgroups); quercetin does not inhibit OCT1 in vitro.
edges.evidence: Meta-analyses (no direct co-administration study) plus in vitro transporter data; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Additive BP lowering: SBP about -2 to -3 mmHg in meta-analyses, larger at >=500 mg/d and in stage 1 hypertension.
edges.evidence: Umbrella review and MAs of RCTs; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Complementary senolytic targets (quercetin: senescent endothelial cells/BM-MSCs; dasatinib: senescent preadipocytes); intermittent D+Q raises AE rates vs placebo.
edges.evidence: Preclinical plus phase 1-2 trials; investigational; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Animal data suggest potentiated nephrotoxicity in damaged kidneys; IV bolus quercetin was dose-limiting nephrotoxic (945-1700 mg/m2).
edges.evidence: Safety review plus phase I IV trial; low certainty for oral doses

edges.mechanism: Animal studies suggest possible promotion of estrogen-dependent tumors.
edges.evidence: Safety review of animal data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Quercetin inhibits iodide uptake, NIS/TSHR/TPO/Tg expression and type 1 deiodinase in vitro and in rats.
edges.evidence: In vitro/rat data and review; no human data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: True physiological lowering via xanthine oxidoreductase inhibition: -26.5 umol/L (CI -7.6 to -45.5) with 500 mg/d for 4 weeks.
edges.evidence: Crossover RCT (n=22) plus mechanistic study; low certainty

edges.mechanism: Quercetin inhibits horseradish peroxidase at nM concentrations, abolishing signal in Amplex-type HRP assays.
edges.evidence: In vitro research-assay data; no clinical analyzer data; very low certainty

edges.mechanism: Quercetin-induced drop in talinolol AUC was most marked in 3435 TT carriers.
edges.evidence: Human PK study (n=18); very low certainty

edges.mechanism: CYP3A induction by quercetin (lower midazolam AUC) more prominent in CYP3A5*1/*1 and *1/*3 carriers.
edges.evidence: Human PK study (n=18); very low certainty
